issue.title: After-rebase import gate counts gitignored .venv .py files as dirty and never certifies

task_type_fields.impact:
The semantic-conflict guard for auto-rebased commits is silently disabled, so
rename/import conflicts can land on master again (the sase-1cb failure class). Fix:
scope the ignored-file query to first-party import roots (`src/`, `tools/`) or exclude
virtualenv directories, then add a regression test with an ignored `.venv/*.py` file.
task_type_fields.repro:
Proposed by phase sase-1tz.4.1.10 note #6; filed by the sase-1tz.4.1 land agent.

Root cause (confirmed on master 39b594a30c): `_python_paths_not_matching_tree`
(`tools/_check_rebase_imports.py:363`) unions four git queries, including
`git ls-files -o -i --exclude-standard`. That query lists every gitignored untracked
file, so every `.py` under `.venv/` and `.venv-format/` counts as "dirty or untracked
.py that could shadow the tree". `_verify_committed_tree` then raises `CheckerError`
(the phase saw "8 shown +3519 more"). Stitch classifies that as an infrastructure error
and publication proceeds with "allowing publication", so the after-rebase import gate
(sase-1pm.5.1 / cddea47cc6) never actually certifies a rebased tree in a real workspace.

Repro: in any sase workspace with a populated `.venv`, run the after-rebase import
checker against the current HEAD tree (or `sase stitch create --resume` after an
auto-rebase) and inspect the run's `commit_hooks/*after_rebase*.json`: it reports the
venv files and an infrastructure error. Evidence: the 20261120174114 run behind
335170e1cb.

issue.creation_reason: Phase sase-1tz.4.1.10 saw the after-rebase import gate fail open on every real workspace during stitch publication; the sase-1tz.4.1 land agent is filing its proposed follow-up.

payload.entry: After-rebase import gate now scopes dirty/untracked .py queries to src/, tools/, and tests/. Regression: ignored .venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/x.py certifies a clean tree; ignored first-party src/sase/ghost.py and untracked src/sase/dirty.py still fail.

LANDING FINDING (sase-1vn land agent, 2026-11-28): the venv fix in f079628697 is correct, but the live gate still mostly fails open, now via timeout. In every after-rebase hook record since the fix (ace-run commit_hooks/*after_rebase*.json), only 2 of 9 publications certified (f079628697 at 1.8s, dcd6c726c3 at 3.0s). The other 7 (324d63e8ef, 1b461588eb, 51fc0d8cb2, 1cde333808, f6dd22d4dd, c783119ffd, 96e87d5984) hit sase/sase.yml after_rebase_timeout_seconds=10 at 9.6s and logged 'after-rebase hook timed out; allowing publication'. Locally on master 8610438838 at load ~4 on 64 cores, the checker took 18.9s, 10.4s, and 7.1s for the changed paths of 96e87d5984, a5fde6cd11, and 8610438838. cProfile of the 18.9s case: about 13s is CommittedTree._entry running a git ls-tree plus a git cat-file subprocess per loaded module (4,412 subprocesses for about 2,200 modules), and 3.4s is compile(). The remaining fix (one recursive ls-tree index plus git blob-hash comparison of worktree bytes, then re-measuring the timeout) is planned as sase-1vn landing work; this bead stays closed and that tale records its verification here.

Rebase-gate speed fix (tale 202611/rebase_gate_speed_and_sase_1vn_closeout): CommittedTree now reads each committed tree once via git ls-tree -r -z --full-tree and verifies worktree bytes by git blob oid hash (sha1/sha256 by oid length), stdlib-only, no per-module subprocesses. Before (live gate, quiet host): 96e87d5984 18.9s, a5fde6cd11 10.4s, 8610438838 7.1s. After (scratch worktree with fix, all status clean): 96e87d5984 4.48s, a5fde6cd11 2.38s, 8610438838 1.78s. Slowest after 4.48s < 5.0s threshold, so after_rebase_timeout_seconds stays 10 (no sase.yml change). New tests: subprocess-count stays 7 (2 rev-parse + 4 dirty + 1 ls-tree) for 30 transitively loaded modules; source_bytes rejects same-length rewrite and retargeted symlink, returns exact bytes when unchanged. Full check run 5bba6f309046f8a180cbb12922b26697 (lint incl. symvision green; test lane still running at note time).
